clue.text: Snap twig

definitions.meaning: as an exclamation of recognition, snap means you see what I mean
to twig is British slang for to grasp or understand

explanation.walkthrough: Both words are verbs meaning to understand; 'snap' is first read as break, as you would a twig.
explanation.definitionFit: Both clue words are informal ways of saying you have understood a situation, an idiom of comprehension.

clue.text: Author denied credit got withers wrung, right?

indicators.note: wrung means twisted, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An uncredited writer has been put through the wringer, the speaker suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter writes books published under another person's name and receives no credit.

clue.text: Chinese secret society descending on a kingdom

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece descends on, so sits above, the next

parts.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society

explanation.surface: A Chinese secret society swoops on a kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonga is a Polynesian island kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a South Pacific monarchy, so it is an example of a kingdom.

clue.text: Attractive fish is excellent

parts.note: hunky means sexually attractive, of a man
the dory is a sea fish, as in John Dory

explanation.surface: A good-looking fish is judged first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is informal for fine or satisfactory, so it means excellent.

clue.text: Friend is no good confined within fences

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: confined within means held inside the next piece

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend is useless once fenced in.
explanation.definitionFit: Palings are fences made of pointed stakes, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Primate in church accompanied by one policeman

indicators.note: accompanied by means joined by, so the pieces follow on

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
MP stands for military policeman

explanation.surface: A senior bishop in church is escorted by a single officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, which fits 'church'; here it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimpanzee is an ape, and apes belong to the primates.

clue.text: Slip maybe beneath the water

parts.note: under means beneath
the Wear is a river in the north east of England

explanation.surface: Someone slips and goes under the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' looks like a fall but is a woman's undergarment; the Wear is a river in County Durham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a petticoat-like garment worn under clothes, an example of underwear.

clue.text: Letter, and when you can hope to receive it.

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet

definitions.text: when you can hope to receive it
definitions.meaning: estimated time of arrival, when post or a visitor is due

explanation.surface: A letter and when it might arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' tempts as post, tying the two halves; in fact one is a Greek letter and the other an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh Greek letter, and ETA abbreviates estimated time of arrival.

clue.text: Blue feathers

definitions.meaning: feeling blue is feeling depressed or low
soft fine feathers as in a duvet filling

explanation.definitionFit: Blue matches the low-spirited sense, and feathers the fluffy plumage sense used for pillows.

clue.text: Girl in the old song Linden Lea performed with energy

indicators.note: a performed piece is worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A singer gives an energetic performance of the folk song Linden Lea.
explanation.walkthrough: LINDEN LEA plus E are rearranged; 'with' is a link. 'Nellie Dean' is an old British music-hall song about a girl of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of a popular music-hall ballad is a girl, so she is the girl in the old song.

clue.text: Calm down! One day it's liable to change (after I quit)

indicators.note: letters liable to change may be reordered, so they are rearranged here

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; the apostrophe adds no letter
the letter that drops out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: Someone urges calm because one day, once a certain person has gone, things will change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After I quit' tells you to drop the I before shuffling what is left; 'liable to change' is the anagram signal, though it reads as a remark about the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations urging someone to stop overreacting and moderate their behaviour.

clue.text: Husband chasing beautiful women will come to grief

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the husband follows the beautiful women

parts.note: peris are beautiful fairy women in Persian legend

explanation.surface: A man who runs after lovely women is warned he will end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: PERI, a fairy of Persian myth, is a crossword staple for a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To perish is to die or be destroyed, the ultimate way of coming to grief.

clue.text: Tweak coppers

definitions.meaning: a tweak is a minor alteration

explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a minor adjustment, and coppers are low-value coins, both senses of the phrase.

clue.text: Gordon Bennett being kind to 18

parts.note: gracious means courteous and kind
the answer to 18 across is a jokey way of saying I, which in the object case is me

explanation.surface: A man named Gordon Bennett treats the writer kindly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gordon Bennett' is a British exclamation of surprise, so it is not a person here; 18 across is YOURS TRULY, a jocular way of saying me.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned British exclamations of astonishment, interchangeable as expletives.

clue.text: A copper's under weight he struggled in the 40's

indicators.note: in a down clue under means placed after the weight

parts.note: a carat is a unit of weight for gems
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, and the possessive gives S

explanation.surface: A copper is underweight and has a struggle on his hands in his forties.
explanation.walkthrough: The 40's are the AD 40s: Caratacus was a British chieftain who resisted the Roman invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Caratacus led British resistance to Rome in the decade after AD 43, so he fought in the 40s.

clue.text: Simple job for academic, making furniture

parts.note: easy means simple
a chair is a professorship

explanation.surface: An undemanding academic post produces some furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a comfortable upholstered armchair, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Nestling they assume is hiding …

indicators.note: is hiding says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A baby bird is supposed to be concealed somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyas is a young hawk taken from the nest, so it is a nestling by definition.

clue.text: … can cause a disturbance

explanation.surface: Something hidden can make trouble, continuing from the clue before.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 16 across for the surface only; 'can' looks like a verb but is prison slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for jail, matching can, and to stir things up is to make a disturbance.

clue.text: I sort slurry out before end of day

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange into order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written as part of the pool

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to clear up a mess of slurry before the day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort ... out' looks like one phrasal verb, but 'out' is part of the fodder: SLURRY plus OUT rearranged gives YOURSTRUL, and the final Y comes from 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yours truly is a jocular way for a speaker to refer to themself, standing in for the first person pronoun.

clue.text: One country or another claiming dominion verbally

parts.note: the UK is a country

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so this word is heard rather than read

parts.note: reign means rule or dominion

explanation.surface: One nation or another lays claim to dominion by speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' completes 'One country or another' and is the definition: another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a country, so it is another country beside the first one named.

clue.text: Free deserter imprisoned by soldiers

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held inside, so the soldiers go around the deserter

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: A captured deserter is released by the soldiers holding him.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means without charge, the same sense as free of cost.

clue.text: Waste open spaces in Paris have turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: parcs is French for parks

explanation.surface: Rubbish has appeared in the parks of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap means discarded material, the same sense as waste.

clue.text: Wrong lecher is about, retrospectively, to redress

indicators.note: is about means goes around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
wrong signals the letters of lecher are put in a wrong order
looking back, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wicked lecher is about to put right past wrongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges the letters to RECLHE, and 'is about' puts that around 'to' turned back. 'Redress' means dress again here, not make amends.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-dress, read as dress again, means putting clothes back on someone, a punning sense.

clue.text: Periodical notes issue from this

definitions.meaning: a magazine or newspaper speaking for a group

explanation.surface: A magazine is where notes are published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes issue' suggests banknotes or memos; here they are musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a party's official newspaper, and also an instrument producing notes.

clue.text: Instrument in a recital earlier

indicators.note: earlier says the recital comes first, before the other words

parts.note: a recital is a musical performance, a concert
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instrument appears in a recital earlier in the programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A concertina is a hand-held bellows instrument with buttons, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Getting on with one's life — drudgery, principally

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, read as the principal or first letters of each word

explanation.surface: Ageing comes with a life mostly of drudgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing advanced in years, which is being aged.

clue.text: Criminals in a group go to Scotland

definitions.meaning: a band of criminals working together
in Scots dialect the verb for to go is ...

explanation.surface: A band of crooks heads off to Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is an organised criminal group, and gang is also the Scots verb meaning go.

clue.text: Lancers perhaps capturing one engineer without a getaway

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the dance surrounds the rest

parts.note: the Lancers is a quadrille, a kind of dance
one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: without means outside, so the engineer goes around the a

parts.note: a sapper is a military engineer

explanation.surface: Cavalry lancers seize an engineer who cannot escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lancers' suggests cavalry but is a dance. 'Without' in its old sense of outside puts SAPPER around A, giving SAPPEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A getaway is an escape, which amounts to a vanishing from the scene.
